Nafaa · Brand exploration · Round 2 · October 2026

Round 2: building on Noon

In round 1, the Noon (ن) was the mark that made sense, so round 2 starts there. Group A develops the Noon in five ways. Group B adds four new marks chosen to be understood in one second, with nothing to explain. Every mark is simple geometry, works in one colour, reads at 16 px, and uses only the brand green and amber. None of them shows a shop, cart, coin or chart.

Round 1 me sirf Noon samajh aaya, is liye round 2 usi se shuru hota hai. Group A: Noon ke paanch roop. Group B: chaar naye nishan jo ek nazar me samajh aa jayein.

A · Noon developments
Noon, boldn + نNoon smileNoon sealNoon, bilingual lockup
B · New, instantly clear
نفع, modernDotted nafaaNoon risingN-Up

Recommendation

  1. A1 · Noon, bold. This is the idea that already landed, made strong enough to be the final mark. The heavier bowl and larger amber nuqta hold up at 16 px, and the meaning (a business, and what it gains) needs no caption. Pair it with the A5 bilingual lockup, "Nafaa | نفع", as the full logo, so it works in Pakistan and abroad from day one.
  2. B3 · Noon rising. The same Noon with its dot turned into an amber up-arrowhead. A green triangle pointing up means "going up" on every price screen in the world, so people get "growth" in one second. Urdu readers still see ن. Choose this one if the owner wants the growth message to be louder than the warmth.

The safest fallback is B4 · N-Up: it is the most literal mark and the most legible at tiny sizes, but arrow marks are common in finance, so it is less ownable.

Meri raaye: A1 Noon bold, saath me A5 wala "Nafaa | نفع" logo. Agar barhat zyada zor se dikhani ho to B3.

How round 2 differs

  • Every mark comes from the one idea that landed (Noon) or must be understood in one second.
  • No abstractions that need a caption: Lift, Exchange and Flow are gone.
  • Each one is tested at 16 px and in one colour (below).
  • Round 1 is kept at the bottom of this page, collapsed, for reference.

Noon, bold Top 1 pick

The ن you liked, made heavier and simpler, with a much larger amber dot above the bowl.

One colour

This is the Noon from round 1 with everything unnecessary removed. The bowl is about 30% heavier, so it holds up at 16 px, and the diamond-shaped dot (the nuqta, as a pen draws it) is nearly twice as big, so the amber reads from across a room. The meaning is plain: the bowl is your business and the dot is what it earns. It is calm, friendly and very easy to recognise on a crowded home screen.

Wohi ن, ab zyada mazboot: bartan aur us me gira hua nafa.

Round 1 · 6 concepts and the refined current markShow

Round 1: a mark for every kind of business

Six new directions for the Nafaa symbol, plus today's mark redrawn as a baseline for comparison. Nafaa serves retail, e-commerce, manufacturing, wholesale and distribution, services and restaurants, so none of these is a picture of a shop. Each is one idea, drawn by hand on a construction grid, and works in one colour. The wordmark is Inter Bold, outlined to paths, so it renders the same everywhere.

Chhe naye nishan, har karobar ke liye. Har ek ko chhote size, dark background aur asal jagah par dekh kar faisla karein.

Ascend NNoonLiftKufic نفعExchangeFlow

Round 1 recommendation (superseded)

  1. 01 · Ascend N. One solid shape that is both the name (an N) and the promise (it climbs up and to the right). It has the cleanest silhouette in the set, stays sharp at 16 px, and engraves, embroiders and prints in one colour without losing anything. It reads the same to a textile mill in Faisalabad and a café in Dubai. It is the safest route to a global, Notion- or Stripe-grade monogram.
  2. 06 · Flow. The most memorable gesture: one unbroken line that draws an n and ends higher than it started, which is "one system" and "growth" in a single stroke. It is the friendliest mark here and the easiest to draw from memory, the way people can draw Airbnb's Bélo. Before adopting it, run a trademark check against Nubank's joined "nu", the closest existing mark.

If the brand should lead with its Pakistani roots, 02 · Noon is the bold alternative: it is the most ownable of all, but it is less obviously "N" to people outside the region.

Next step: show the top two to 8 to 10 owners from different industries on a phone home screen. Ask what they see, and which one they can still describe the next day.

Meri raaye: Ascend N sab se mazboot aur saaf hai; Flow sab se yaadgaar hai.

Today's mark, for comparison

→

The current diagonal runs from bottom-left to top-right, so the letter is a mirrored N ("И"). The refined version fixes this, but it is still a letter with a dot. It is shown only as a baseline, not as a recommendation.

01

Ascend N

A solid geometric N whose right stem climbs higher than the left, so the name itself moves upward.

One colour

One closed shape on a 32 px grid. The left stem is short, the right stem is tall, and both tops are cut on the same rising 1:2 angle, so the N climbs up and to the right as you read it. That is the whole idea: Nafaa means profit, and the letter itself rises. It has no curves and no extra parts, so it stays sharp from a 16 px favicon to a sign on a factory gate, and it embosses, engraves and stitches cleanly. Like Notion's N or Stripe's S, it is a monogram the brand can own.

N jo khud upar ki taraf barhta hai: naam bhi, rukh bhi.

02

Noon

The letter ن, the first letter of نفع: an open vessel with the dot of gain held above it.

One colour

ن is a bowl with one dot above it. Read as a symbol, the bowl is any business, open and ready to receive, and the amber dot is what it gains. The bowl is drawn from two offset circles, so it is heavy at the base and thins towards the tips the way a reed pen draws it, and the left tip is cut on the pen's angle. Urdu and Arabic readers see "noon" straight away, and everyone else sees a simple, friendly abstract form. No business app owns this letter yet. It pairs with a lowercase "nafaa", whose n is the same arch turned over.

نفع ka pehla harf "noon": khula bartan, aur upar uska nafa.

03

Lift

A circle split in two with its right half raised: the whole business, with its gain lifted.

One colour

A circle stands for the whole: one business, one system. Split it down the middle and raise the right half, and you have the simplest possible picture of growth, built from two perfect semicircles and nothing else. The step between the halves gives it movement, and the amber half makes the gain visible. It is the most abstract concept here, so it suits a bakery, a garment exporter and a software agency equally well. It is also easy to animate: the right half rises as the app loads.

Ek poora daira, jiska ek hissa upar uth gaya: yahi nafa hai.

04

Kufic نفع

The whole word نفع set in square Kufic on a 9 x 6 module grid, like a firm's seal (mohr).

One colour

Square Kufic is a centuries-old way of writing Arabic script with pure squares. Trading houses, workshops and firms across the region have always stamped their name with a seal, and this mark is that seal made modern. Here ن, ف and ع sit on one baseline built from equal square modules, and the two amber diamonds are the letters' dots (the nuqte). It has the strongest local identity of the set and looks excellent on invoices, packaging and signage. The trade-off is that at 16 px it becomes a texture rather than a word, so it would need a simpler favicon.

Poora lafz نفع, chokor Kufi khat me, jaise kisi firm ki mohar.

05

Exchange

An N made of two identical strokes that reach towards each other: every business is two sides meeting.

One colour

Buyer and seller, supplier and maker, business and customer: every kind of business is two sides meeting. This N is built from two identical hooked strokes, one turned 180 degrees, which run towards each other along the diagonal and stop just short of touching. The small gap in the centre is the moment of exchange. Because the mark is rotationally symmetric, it feels balanced and engineered, and the amber half shows the side that gains. A monogram built this way is unusual, which makes it memorable, and it still reads as N at every size.

Do barabar hisse jo beech me milte hain: har karobar len-den hai.

06

Flow

One unbroken line that draws an n, dips, and ends higher than it began: one system, always moving up.

One colour

Nafaa is one system for the whole business: purchasing, stock, production, sales and accounts. This mark is a single continuous stroke that never lifts. It draws the arch of a lowercase n, dips into a curve, and finishes above the point where it started. In one gesture it shows flow (everything connected) and growth (the end is higher than the start). Like Wise's flag or Airbnb's Bélo, it is a line you could draw from memory with a finger. It works equally well as a solid tile or as a bare line on a dark screen.

Ek hi lakeer: n banati hai, neeche aati hai, aur shuru se zyada upar nikal jati hai.

00

Current mark, refined Baseline only

Comparison baseline only: today's N-and-dot, redrawn so the N reads the right way.

One colour

This is not a new direction. It is here so the new concepts can be judged against what Nafaa uses today. The current icon draws its diagonal from bottom-left to top-right, so the letter is a mirrored N (it reads as "И"). This version keeps the green tile, the white rounded strokes and the amber dot, fixes the letter and lets the right stem rise slightly. It is cleaner than today's mark, but it is still a letter with a dot, which is not distinctive enough to carry a global brand.

Sirf muqable ke liye: purana nishan, bas saaf aur durust.
